title: The session identifier in an SRP exchange is built from a timestamp, so the shared key can be recomputed instead of proven
index_line: T-0097 · AUTH_DECISION · vmdir SRP-6a over DCE/RPC: UUIDv1-derived session id → session key recovered without a password · cpp · corroborated
invariant_violated: SRP assumes the session material it derives is unpredictable to an observer: the shared key is only ever *proven*, never transmitted. When the session identifier is generated from a UUIDv1 — a timestamp plus a MAC — the material is guessable within a window, so the key can be computed by an unauthenticated peer and the proof of password knowledge becomes unnecessary.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated attacker opens an SRP-6a authentication exchange with vmdir over the DCE/RPC interface on port 2012
the server answers with its SRP challenge, which carries the session identifier the pair will derive keys from
that identifier was generated from a UUIDv1 — a timestamp plus a MAC-derived node — so the attacker learns its structure from the challenge
the timestamp component narrows the identifier to an enumerable window, so the shared session key is recomputed instead of proven
the key is derived by the attacker, so the credential proof the protocol relies on never has to be satisfied
an authenticated session is established as administrator@vsphere.local
the vmdirdbcp RPC interface is used to run commands and read data.mdb, the directory's credential store

source.protocol.value: the vmdir DCE/RPC authentication interface (TCP 2012): SRP-6a handshake frames

guard.signature.value: the SRP key-proof step that is replaced by recomputation because the session material is predictable

sink.file.read.value: the data.mdb directory database read through vmdirdbcp once administrator@vsphere.local is held

oracle.channel.value: the recovered session key itself is the oracle — a successful session proves the recomputation worked

preconditions.expr: the vmdir RPC authentication service is reachable (TCP 2012)

check.spec: timeout 5 bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/HOST/2012 && echo open || echo closed'; curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://HOST/sdk
curl -sk https://HOST/sdk/vimServiceVersions.xml | head -c 200; printf 'version also in the vSphere Client About box\n'

preconditions.expr: the directory service derives SRP session material from a UUIDv1

success: an authenticated vSphere session as administrator@vsphere.local without any credential
subsequent vmdirdbcp calls returning directory data or executing commands
failure_like: the build generates the session identifier from a CSPRNG and rejects recomputation
port 2012 is not reachable from the attacker's position
false_positive: a successful anonymous SOAP call to /sdk is not this bug — require an authenticated session object
log entries showing failed SRP attempts are the handshake, not the compromise

hazards: any PAKE/SRP/challenge-response exchange whose nonce or session id comes from a time-based generator
UUIDv1 is a timestamp in disguise: it is an identifier, never a secret
the recovered key yields the highest-privilege directory identity, so the bypass lands as administrator
non_transfers: exchanges that use CSPRNG nonces and bind them into the key derivation
services that do not expose the authentication RPC to untrusted networks

evidence.target: VMware vCenter Server, VMware Directory Service (vmdir) SRP over DCE/RPC (CVE-2026-123890, ARMORY CASTLE)

provenance.author: Google Threat Intelligence / Mandiant (ARMORY CASTLE)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-123890: unauthenticated SRP-6a session-key disclosure over DCE/RPC on port 2012, exploiting predictable UUIDv1 timestamp generation in the SRP authentication interface; the shared session key is recovered without any password, producing a session as administrator@vsphere.local, then vmdirdbcp is used to run commands and exfiltrate data.mdb
